subject: geography
title: Weather and climate
objective: Tell weather apart from climate and name the controls on each.

lesson.opening: Weather is what the sky is doing now; climate is the long-run pattern of weather in a place.

sections.heading: Two timescales
sections.body: Weather changes hour to hour. Climate is the average and the range of conditions over decades. A cold week does not disprove a warming climate.

sections.heading: Controls on climate
sections.body: Latitude sets how much sunlight a place receives. Altitude cools the air. Distance from the sea moderates temperature. Ocean currents warm or cool coasts, and prevailing winds carry moisture or dryness.

sections.heading: Oceans and climate
sections.body: A warm current can keep a high-latitude port ice-free; a cold current can help create a coastal desert.

activities.prompt: Which factor cools a place at high altitude?
Why are coastal places often milder than inland places?
choices: They are closer to the equator

activities.prompt: Explain how one control on climate shapes a place you know.
activities.instructions: Name the control and the effect.
activities.context: Latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, currents, and winds all shape local climate.
